## What this PR does

One or two sentences. If the PR fixes an existing issue, link it: `Fixes #N` / `Closes #N`.

## Why

What problem does this solve, and why is this approach the right one? For non-trivial changes please reference any prior discussion in the linked issue.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes a documented or observed defect)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change that adds capability)
- [ ] Breaking change (alters existing behavior; requires major-version bump and CHANGELOG entry)
- [ ] Documentation only
- [ ] Performance improvement (no functional change)
- [ ] Internal refactor (no user-visible change)
- [ ] CI / tooling

## Non-negotiables check

`holotype` has six non-negotiables documented in `SKILL.md`. Confirm none of these are softened by this PR:

- [ ] Forensic completeness (no filtering of transcript content)
- [ ] Provenance via hash chain (SHA-256 per session, verifiable with stock Unix tools)
- [ ] Git is the archive substrate
- [ ] Environment capture (host CLI version, OS, holotype version, project-repo git state)
- [ ] Append-only by design
- [ ] No silent network behavior

If any box is unchecked, this PR needs explicit prior discussion in an issue and approval to soften the rule.

## Selftest

- [ ] `python scripts/selftest.py` passes locally
- [ ] If this PR adds a feature or fixes a bug, a new selftest assertion exercises the change
- [ ] CI is green (GitHub Actions workflow on this PR)

## Manifest / archive-format impact

- [ ] No archive-format change
- [ ] `manifest_version` bumped from N to N+1 (note: existing archives will auto-re-process on next ingest via the manifest-version-mismatch path)
- [ ] `index_schema_version` bumped from N to N+1 (note: existing indexes will be auto-rebuilt)
- [ ] On-disk archive layout changed (describe migration path)

If any archive-format box is checked, also update `docs/project_schema_versions` (the memory entry equivalent if maintained) and add a CHANGELOG entry.
